summary: A tight, puzzly worker-placement-adjacent Euro where you race around a rondel-like action track to gather resources and place them on angled garden boards to determine ingredient quality, then brew barrels scored by their weakest ingredient. It plays fast for its depth, with constant tension between rushing to grab good rondel spots and taking time to upgrade your garden.
praised: Elegant, tightly interlocking systems for a mid-weight game
Clever tile-tilting garden mechanic that rewards spatial planning
Fast turns and low downtime despite meaningful depth
High replayability from varied strategies and player counts
Satisfying puzzle of optimizing barrel quality before scoring
criticised: Barrel scoring uses lowest-value-counts-most, which can feel punishing or fiddly to track
Rondel/turn-order tension can create early-game analysis paralysis
Some randomness in resource/tile availability can swing outcomes
Theme feels pasted on rather than integrated

interaction.kind: turn-order and rondel-spot claiming, indirect competition for shared resources

scoring.why: Points come from barrel quality (bounded by the weakest ingredient), garden expansion, and bonus track progress, so efficient balancing across a few interlocking systems decides the winner
